<thought>We need to determine the number of aromatic carbons in the molecule, but we have no explicit structure. The available tools can provide NMR spectra for the sample at hand, which likely includes the molecule. By retrieving the 13C NMR spectrum, we can count the signals in the aromatic region (typically ~110-160 ppm). This will give the number of distinct aromatic carbon environments, which for a typical aromatic ring equals the number of aromatic carbons if all are chemically equivalent or distinct. We'll retrieve the carbon NMR spectrum and count the aromatic region peaks.</thought>
<action>carbon_nmr_spectra</action>
